newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Captall sees strong full yr perfomance.
newsitem.headline: Captall sees strong full yr perfomance.

text.p: Capital Alliance Holdings Ltd (Captall) said on Friday it was pleased with its interim performance and would post strong results for the full year.
During the six months to end September, 1996, Captall bought Capital Alliance Bank (formerly NDH Bank Ltd), Capital Alliance Securities (formerly Ryan Anderson Ltd) and Capital Alliance Ltd.

"While the figures for the current period are therefore not fully comparable with the previous period, it is clear that Capital Alliance has nevertheless experienced an outstanding six months," Captall chairman Mzi Khumalo said at the release of results.
He said profitability achieved in the first half would continue in the second half.
Captall is a financial services group involved in corporate, and merchant banking, stockbroking, asset management and the life assurance and pensions business.
Asked of the progress to bid for Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd's 35 percent stake in JCI Ltd Khumalo said:
"We have pointed out that we are not... changing to a mining house. We might get together with other black groups. We are waiting."
Captall raised interim share by 35 percent to 35.1 cents from 26.0 cents. Attributable income was raised to 25.02 million rand from 10.96 million rand previously.
No interim dividend was declared as it is company policy to declare a single dividend at year end.
Mark Barnes, chief executive officer of Captall, said their objective was to create a broadly based, fully South African financial services group.

He said the bank would be rapidly built to a fully capable merchant bank, focused on lending and deposit-taking. Capital Alliance Life, the insurance unit, would seek further growth through selective acquisition and product expansion.
Barnes said the investment counsel business was in start-up phase and was seen breaking even for the full year.
The business would be expanded through the launching of new investment vehicles and industry specialisation in fund management, he said.
Barnes said the aim was to aggressively look for expansion avenues in order to reach critical mass.
"Our intention is to be fit, aware and hungry, seeking out opportunities that present themselves," he said.
